questions: Should the function process only regular files, or also directories and other special files (symlinks, devices) that appear in glob.glob('*')?
If a file in source_dir cannot be opened (e.g., permission denied), should the function raise an exception, skip that file, or halt entirely?
Should the hash be computed on the raw bytes of the file (as read in binary mode) or on the decoded text content (as read in 'r' mode)?
Should the target directory be created if it does not exist, or should the function raise an error?
Should the function preserve the original file's newline endings when writing the modified content?
If a file in source_dir is empty (zero bytes), should the hash be computed on an empty string, and should the output file contain only the hash line?
Should the function follow symbolic links in source_dir to hash the linked file's content, or treat the symlink itself as a file?
Should the order of the returned list of paths match any specific order (e.g., alphabetical, creation time, glob order), or is any order acceptable as long as all files are included?
